content: Sweet violet, scientifically known as Viola odorata, is a plant species belonging to the genus Viola. It is native to Europe and Asia but has also been introduced to North America. This plant is commonly referred to as the Garden Violet. Viola odorata can be differentiated from other violet species by several distinct characteristics. Firstly, its flowers emit a sweet fragrance. The flowers are typically dark violet or white in color. Both the leaves and flowers grow in a basal rosette arrangement. The style of the flower is hooked and does not terminate in a rounded appendage. Additionally, the leaf stalks are covered with hairs that point downward. The plant propagates through stolons, which are above-ground shoots. Sweet violet is often found growing near the edges of forests or in clearings. It is also a frequent, unintentional presence in shaded lawns or other areas within gardens. The flowers of this species begin to bloom as early as February and continue until the end of April.
